newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond supply simmers down, see IFC in sterling.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond supply simmers down, see IFC in sterling.

text.p: ** The primary market saw a winding down of supply on
Thursday afternoon as January drew to a close.
** IFC set a 250 million stg 3-year bond via Yamaichi.
** Lehman Brothers priced a $150 million FRN for First
Maryland at three-month LIBOR plus 85 basis points.
** In the emerging market sector, Sao Paulo state power
company Cesp aims to launch a $200 million Eurobond in March.
Russia plans to issue its second Eurobond in two or three
Sterling supply, which has doubled in January this year versus the same period last year, saw another deal launched in afternoon trade.
All international bonds in sterling totalled $12.51 billion equivalent in January 1997 versus $6.06 billion in the same month last year, according to Capital DATA Bondware.
The triple-A rated International Finance Corporation (IFC) launched a 250 million stg three-year Eurobond which pays a coupon of 6.34 percent.
"Sterling has been the arbitrage currency this year, its a high-yield currency," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
Syndicate manager at Yamaichi -- lead manager of the IFC transaction -- said the paper was targeted at Japanese retail investors who were always hungry for yield.
"The deal follows the Finland deal we did earlier this month," she said. Finland launched a 150 million stg three-year bond which paid a coupon of 6.78 percent.
Sao Paulo state power company Cesp aims to launch a $200 million Eurobond in March, the first tranche of a $500 million debt programme for this year, Cesp spokesman Octavio de Barros said.

Russia plans to launch its second Eurobond issue in two or three months and two more issues will appear in the second half of the year, Interfax news agency quoted a Finance Ministry official as saying on Thursday.
Deputy head of the foreign credits department Vladimir Dmitriyev said the second issue would most likely be in marks.
